title: CoreWeave CEO Sold $907M of Stock in 2026 Before Calling 25% Rout Irrational

tickers.name: CoreWeave, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
SEC filings show CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator has sold $907 million of the AI cloud provider's stock in 2026, while early backer Magnetar Capital has offloaded more than $5.5 billion of shares since the March 2025 IPO. Together with co-founders Brian Venturo and Brannin McBee, the three executives have sold $3.3 billion in stock since going public, including $2.4 billion this year, making Venturo the second-largest insider seller at any US company in 2026. Since mid-August alone, CoreWeave insiders have sold $302 million in shares with zero purchases, led by $199 million from Intrator.

The insider sales contrast with an internal memo earlier this week in which Intrator told employees that "there will be periods of time when the market misunderstands and acts irrationally" as CoreWeave shares fell 12% on Friday to bring their weekly loss to 25%. The rout centered on the company's roughly $50 billion in debt and lease obligations, with yields on its unsecured bonds topping 15% and five year credit default swaps reaching a record 1,194.5 basis points, implying a more than 60% probability of default within five years alongside $7.5 billion of debt coming due by June 2027.

While unsecured bondholders price in distress, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said on Thursday that CoreWeave does not need a backstop and that its cost of capital is "actually decreasing." Project-finance facilities backed by specific GPU clusters and customer contracts make up the majority of CoreWeave's debt, and pricing on those delayed-draw term loans tightened from 9.62 percentage points over the benchmark rate in 2023 to 2.25 percentage points in March 2026, before widening to 5.50 percentage points on a five year facility in July backed by three year contracts with non-investment-grade customers.

selectedTweets.text:
Should be pretty evident CoreWeave's cost of capital is declining over any timeframe greater than a few months.. DDTLs (the ABS, project-finance style facilities backed by specific clusters and customer contracts) comprise the majority of CoreWeave's debt.

Pricing on the DDTLs has tightened a lot over the years. From S+9.62% for DDTL 1.0 issued in 2023..  to as low as S+2.25% for DDTL 4.0 done in March 2026. Note how the older, higher-priced DDTLs 1.0 and 2.0 are declining as the facilities are fully self-amortizing.. And new, lower-priced DDTLs are drawn to fund the most recent capex. 

Will be interesting to see where the next DDTL prices. Not going to argue it will be tighter than the S+2.25% (DDTL 4.0) and S+4.50% (5.0) prints from earlier this year. But probably worth noting that DDTL 5.5 was done at S+5.50% (not shown below as it was completed post quarter-end) in July 2026 when AI financing markets were similarly volatile.. And DDTL 5.5 has a 5 year term yet funds capex associated with non-investment grade customers on 3 year contracts, making it a much more aggressive structure than anything prior. In any event, where DDTL 6.0 lands seems much more important than where its (illiquid) unsecured senior notes are trading.

COREWEAVE BONDS REBOUND SHARPLY AFTER RECENT SELLOFF

CoreWeave ($CRWV ) bonds are recovering as buying returns following a sharp selloff driven by concerns over the company's debt.

The October 2031 bonds jumped 3.3 cents to 82.8 cents on the dollar, while the June 2030 bonds surged 5.7 cents to 91.3 cents.

The rebound suggests some easing in credit market pressure, although both bonds remain below face value.
